body_markdown:

**TLDR:**


-


Wispr Flow works well for individual reps but lacks shared dictionaries, admin controls, and Windows support for sales teams


-


The latency gap matters more than it sounds: Willow Voice processes at ~200ms vs. Wispr Flow's ~700ms across a full day of CRM updates and follow-ups


-


Shared custom dictionaries let your whole team load product names and deal terminology once, so every rep transcribes consistently from day one


-


Wispr Flow's pricing is structured around individual users, so team deployment, admin visibility, and compliance coverage can raise the effective cost


-


Willow Voice is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant with zero data retention architecture, built for teams selling into compliance-sensitive industries

## Speed and Accuracy Inside the Sales Day


A sales rep's day runs on speed. Qualification calls, follow-up emails, CRM updates, proposal notes: each one a small tax on time that compounds across a team of twenty. The[Salesforce State of Sales](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/state-of-sales/sales-statistics/) report finds that reps spend only about 30% of their week actually selling, with admin tasks, CRM logging, and follow-up documentation accounting for the rest.[Stanford research on speech vs. typing](https://hci.stanford.edu/research/speech/paper/speech_paper.pdf) puts average speaking speed at roughly three times average typing speed, which means the ceiling on voice gains is real, but only if the tool keeps up and the output requires minimal correction.


Willow's ~200ms latency keeps text appearing fast enough that the next thought doesn't stall. For enterprise sales teams, that speed advantage compounds across distributed orgs where reps work on Windows desktops, MacBooks, and phones throughout the day. More relevant still, the shared custom dictionary lets revenue ops or an enablement lead load in approved terminology once, covering product names, objection-handling phrases, and competitor references, and every rep in the org transcribes consistently from day one regardless of device or location.


That gap between gross speed and net speed matters here. A tool that transcribes at ~700ms and requires manual correction on proper nouns trades one kind of friction for another. For a full[Willow vs Wispr Flow](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/wisprflow) breakdown, see our dedicated comparison. When domain vocabulary is pre-loaded and accuracy runs high enough that the correction loop shrinks to near zero, voice input yields a real time gain over typing, not because the tool is faster in isolation, but because the rework disappears.

Willow's shared custom dictionaries let teams load that vocabulary once and distribute it org-wide. A new rep recording their first call recap by voice gets the same transcription accuracy as someone six months in. Team leaderboards surface usage and time-saved data across the group, giving revenue leaders visibility into where voice adoption is taking hold and where reps are still typing through tasks they could be handling with voice. Admin controls and org-wide deployment are built into the product from the ground up, not added after the fact. Sales teams running across Windows workstations and MacBooks work from the same vocabulary and configuration without per-device setup, which matters most for IT teams managing a mixed-device fleet during rollout.


## Privacy, Compliance, and Security for Sales Teams


Sales conversations carry sensitive information. Prospect pain points, deal structures, pricing discussions, competitive intelligence shared under NDA; the audio flowing through a dictation tool during a rep's workday is not generic data.[Gartner's enterprise AI adoption research](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-08-26-gartner-predicts-40-percent-of-enterprise-apps-will-feature-task-specific-ai-agents-by-2026-up-from-less-than-5-percent-in-2025) predicts that 40% of enterprise applications will include task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, making how those tools handle security, compliance, and deployment a central procurement question for IT and sales leadership. For a full look at[voice dictation security and privacy](https://willowvoice.com/blog/voice-dictation-security-privacy-guide) , see our dedicated guide.


Wispr Flow is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, which covers most general business requirements. For standard B2B sales teams, that baseline is likely sufficient.


Where the tools diverge is in how compliance is built into the product itself. Willow Voice is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant, with zero data retention as a baseline architectural property across every plan tier, not a paid upgrade or enterprise negotiation. For sales teams operating in healthcare, financial services, or other compliance-sensitive verticals, that distinction matters during procurement: the tool handling your audio is already built for those constraints, not retrofitted to meet them, and it clears enterprise security review without initiating a separate compliance review cycle.


On the team management side, Wispr Flow offers individual-level privacy controls but has no publicly documented enterprise admin console or org-level usage visibility. Willow's admin controls let IT teams and sales managers configure deployment settings, manage users, and roll out shared vocabulary across the org from a central dashboard, whether reps are on Windows workstations or MacBooks, without relying on each rep to configure their own setup correctly.

## FAQs


### **Is Wispr Flow compatible with Salesforce and HubSpot?**


Yes. Wispr Flow works across standard web-based text fields, which includes HubSpot and Salesforce. Willow Voice works the same way across any text field system-wide, with no per-tool plugins required.


### **Does Willow Voice work on Windows for sales teams?**


Yes, natively. Willow supports Windows with full feature parity alongside Mac, making it a practical fit for sales teams running mixed-device environments where not every rep is on the same hardware.


### **Does Willow Voice integrate with CRMs?**


Willow operates as a system-wide dictation layer across any app or text field, including Salesforce, HubSpot, and Outreach, without requiring native integrations or per-tool plugins beyond installing the app.


## Final Thoughts on Wispr Flow vs. Willow Voice for Sales Teams


[Wispr Flow for sales teams](https://willowvoice.com/) works well enough at the individual level; if your reps are on Mac and mostly work alone, the basics are covered. But for a sales org that needs consistent terminology across every rep from day one, admin visibility into adoption, and compliance coverage that holds up in high-stakes deals, the gap between the two tools is real and compounds quickly.
